question: The Braille System is based on:
solution:
The correct answer is __**dots**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Braille system is a tactile writing system used by people who are visually impaired.
 
• It is traditionally written with embossed paper and consists of raised dots.
 
• Each Braille character or cell is made up of six dots arranged in a rectangle containing two columns of three dots each.
 
• The arrangement of these dots represents different letters and symbols used in written language.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Braille System:**

 
 
• Named after its creator, Louis Braille, who developed the system in 1824.
 
• Braille is used worldwide and has been adapted to different languages.
 
• It includes not just letters and punctuation, but also numeric symbols, musical notation, and computer notation.
 
• Learning Braille allows visually impaired individuals to read and write independently, providing access to education, employment, and information.
 
 
 
• **Louis Braille:**
 
 
• Born in 1809 in France, Louis Braille lost his sight at a young age due to an accident.
 
• He was a student at the Royal Institute for Blind Youth in Paris where he developed the Braille system.
 
• The system was based on a tactile military code called "night writing" developed by Charles Barbier.
 
• Louis Braille's system was officially adopted by the Institute in 1854, two years after his death.
 
 
 
• **Usage of Braille:**
 
 
• Braille is used in many areas including education, literature, and public spaces.
 
• Books, menus, signs, and even currency in some countries have Braille for accessibility.
 
• Technology advancements have led to Braille displays and printers, which allow visually impaired individuals to interact with digital information.
 
• Braille literacy is crucial for the independence and empowerment of individuals with visual impairments.
 
 
 
• **Modern Adaptations:**
 
 
• Electronic Braille devices like Braille e-books, Braille watches, and Braille note-takers are becoming more common.
 
• These devices help in accessing digital content and communication for visually impaired individuals.
 
• Braille transcription services convert printed text into Braille for educational and informational purposes.
 
• Efforts continue globally to promote Braille literacy and ensure accessibility in public and private sectors.
